title: Linux - The Warp "Cut All Left" keyboard shortcut does not appear to do anything
body:
### Discord username (optional)

_No response_

### Describe the bug

The `Cut All Left` keyboard shortcut does not appear to do anything when pressed.

I wanted to unbind `Ctrl+U` from `Copy and Clear Selected Lines` and bind it to `Cut All Left`, but I also tried other bindings to no avail.

### To reproduce

1. Open settings
2. Navigate to Keyboard shortcuts
3. Search the commands for "Cut All Left"
4. Bind to `<unused-keybind>` (or Ctrl + U, and unbind it from "Copy and Clear Selected Lines")
5. Close settings
6. Type some characters at terminal prompt
7. Move cursor left (To ensure its only removing characters from the left rather than whole line)
8. Press bound key

### Expected behavior

All characters left of the cursor should be cut/deleted.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system and version

Fedora 39

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9

### Current Warp version

v0.2024.03.12.08.02.stable_01

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

I'm using X11 and I have the following in my `.zshrc`:

```zsh
bindkey \^u backward-kill-line
```

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this a Warp specific issue? (i.e. does it happen in Terminal, iTerm, Kitty, etc.)

Yes, this I confirmed this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.
